name: Federal ban on non-Canadians buying residential property
name_fr: Interdiction d'achat d'immeubles résidentiels par des non-Canadiens
description: Federal law prohibits most non-Canadians from buying residential property in Canada until 1 January 2027, with exemptions that include some work-permit holders and properties outside census metropolitan areas and census agglomerations.

attributes.jurisdiction: federal (applies in every province; provincial taxes on foreign buyers are separate — Agent 02)
attributes.legal_status: in force; scheduled to end 1 January 2027 after the two-year extension in Budget Implementation Act 2024 (Bill C-69); no further extension found on 2026-10-30
attributes.who_is_affected: Non-Canadians — people who are neither Canadian citizens nor permanent residents (plus certain corporations)
attributes.work_permit_holders_exemption: Exempt if at least 183 days remain on the work permit or work authorization on the purchase date and the person has not bought more than one residential property (2023 amendments; earlier Canadian work-experience and tax-filing conditions repealed)
other_exemptions: Residential property outside a census metropolitan area or census agglomeration
Other categories in the Regulations not catalogued here (e.g. some students, refugees, spouses of Canadians)
attributes.status_dependency: Whether the user may buy depends on status at purchase (citizen, PR, work-permit holder or none) — unknown (USER-PROFILE.md).
